prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I moved my own first choice, base editing (B058), into a two-part configuration with Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B057), because the opening ballots show B057 is the best-supported and most mature candidate on the table (three first places, about three decades of independent confirmation, routine use in process chemistry). It also has a clean principle: ligand-controlled catalysis that makes a bond chemists previously could not form generally. Base editing is the second pillar. It converts one base pair into another by engineered deaminase chemistry with no double-strand break, so there is a defined chemical mechanism, a genuinely new capability, a decade of independent replication, and first clinical use. Both parts can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence each, and they are different in kind (synthetic methodology and chemical biology), which makes the pairing a fair reflection of the breadth of chemistry. Restricting the base-editing part to Liu keeps the union at three people and avoids a contested split of the first-author credit.
statement.case_against: The main reservation is that a two-part prize forces a narrow credit on each part. Base editing is only about ten years old, long-term clinical safety is still accruing, and CRISPR-Cas9 was recognised in 2020, so a reader may see it as a derivative of that prize. Omitting Komor and Gaudelli, who carried out the decisive experiments, and Nishida and Kondo, who worked independently on cytidine deamination, is a real judgment, not a neutral one. For B057, Kosugi's earlier tin-amide chemistry is a recognised priority complication that a two-name citation sidesteps rather than resolves.

responses.point: B057 is straightforward, enabling chemistry with demonstrated consequences, and a Buchwald-Hartwig pair is a clean, defensible configuration; Kosugi is a precursor conceptually distinct from the general catalytic method.
responses.response: I agree on the pair and I have changed my view because of this: I had ranked B057 outside my top three on the grounds of elegance, but your emphasis on consequences, together with the unanimity of the three first-place ballots on the same two names, persuades me it should anchor the configuration. I would qualify one point. Calling Kosugi merely a precursor needs the committee to examine what he did with tin amides and what the later ligand work added. I will not support a citation that overstates novelty, so the wording should say 'development of the general palladium-catalyzed' coupling.

responses.point: Buchwald and Hartwig independently made the ligand-enabled, general catalytic amination, and the Migita/Kosugi priority question is the one complication; the field is mature and arguably overdue after the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: Your point on priority is the one I most want settled before the final ballot. As a physicist I cannot judge the synthetic literature myself, so I ask you to state concretely what the 1983 tin-amide work could not do that the 1994-1995 and later ligand systems could, so that the citation can separate original discovery from refinement. I also take your point that 2010 left this branch unrecognised, which is why I do not regard overlap with that prize as a bar.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B004) is a new therapeutic modality, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the cleanest trio and the cereblon glue strand as a second strand.
responses.response: I take the design principle seriously and keep B004 as my first alternative. I disagree that the three-name trio is cleaner than my choices: the PROTAC concept and the thalidomide-cereblon glue mechanism are two distinct discoveries with different people (Handa, Ito), and no degrader has yet been approved, so the clinical evidence that you yourself call possibly premature is still thin. If the committee wants a degradation prize, I would want an explicit decision on whether it honours the concept, the glue mechanism or both before the names are chosen.

responses.point: Biomolecular condensates (B051) are a new concept of molecular organisation grounded in multivalency and phase behaviour, with Brangwynne and Hyman showing liquid-like P granules and Rosen supplying the physical-chemical framework.
responses.response: This was my second choice and I share your reading of the physics, but I put it as an alternative, not in the preferred configuration, because of the maturity question you acknowledge: it is roughly fifteen years old, and which in-cell assemblies are truly phase-separated remains disputed. Pappu and Mittag also make a three-person line contestable. I would like you to say which of the in-vivo claims you consider settled, since that determines whether the citation can name a mechanism rather than a concept.

responses.point: Base editors (B058) are a chemical solution to genome editing, with Liu as intellectual leader and Komor and Gaudelli as trainees; he notes that a Liu-only prize would also be defensible, that CRISPR was recognised in 2020, and that off-target deamination and long-term outcomes remain open.
responses.response: We broadly agree on the science, and your concern about timing is the strongest argument against my own pick. I answer it as follows: the chemistry of deamination is distinct from the nuclease cleavage honoured in 2020, and the independent replication and first clinical data are already in hand. I take up your Liu-only suggestion in the configuration, because it avoids deciding between Komor, Gaudelli and Nishida and Kondo while staying within the three-person limit. I do not claim the safety question is closed, and I would accept that as a reason for the committee to defer B058 if others find it persuasive.

uncertainties: Whether Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling is a precursor or a co-discovery, and whether that should change the citation or the number of B057 names
Whether base editing is mature enough, given that long-term clinical safety and off-target deamination data are still accruing
Whether a Liu-only credit for B058 is acceptable, or whether Komor, Gaudelli or Nishida and Kondo deserve inclusion, which would cost a place in a two-part prize
Whether a two-part prize with B057 is preferred by colleagues over a single-achievement prize such as B057 alone or B004
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: I have no stated connection to any candidate on the shortlist. I share Lund University affiliation with committee colleagues Somfai and Sparr, but this is not a conflict with any shortlisted candidate.
